cards.explanation: The answer is True. Jonathan is named right there, along with his brothers Abinadab and Malchishua. The verse says the Philistines “…killed Saul’s sons Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua.” (1 Chronicles 10:2) Saul was Israel's king, so this lands on his whole family. I think this is a quiet, hard line to read, friends.

Saul asks his armor-bearer to run him through with a sword. He tells him, “Draw your sword and run me through with it…” (1 Chronicles 10:4) The archers have already wounded him, and the Philistines are closing in. This is a very heavy moment, friends, so I'll just say it plainly.

The word is torture. Saul says the “…uncircumcised men will come and torture me!” (1 Chronicles 10:4) That's what he's afraid of as the Philistines close in. I think that tells us how scared he is. It's a heavy verse, friends.

The answer is False. The text says the armor-bearer “…was terrified and refused to do it.” (1 Chronicles 10:4) Saul asked, and he would not. Then Saul took his own sword. This is one of the heaviest spots in the passage, friends.

The armor-bearer falls on his own sword too. The verse says that when he “…saw that Saul was dead, he too fell on his own sword and died.” (1 Chronicles 10:5) The text doesn't tell us what he was thinking, so I won't guess. I'll just say it's a sad line, friends. Chronicles reports it and moves on.

The Israelites abandon their cities and run. The Israelites in the valley saw the army had fled and that Saul and his sons were dead, so they “…abandoned their cities and ran away.” (1 Chronicles 10:7) I think that's a scary moment, friends. The king is gone and the army has fled.

The word is occupy. The verse says the Philistines “…came and occupied their cities.” (1 Chronicles 10:7) The Israelites ran, and the Philistines moved right into the empty towns. That's a big loss for Israel, friends.

The answer is False. The Philistines “…sent messengers throughout the land of the Philistines to proclaim the news in the temple of their idols and among their people.” (1 Chronicles 10:9) The news went out across their whole land. They kept nothing quiet, friends.

The men of valor bring back the bodies of Saul and his sons. All their men of valor “…set out and retrieved the bodies of Saul and his sons and brought them to Jabesh.” (1 Chronicles 10:12) They heard what had been done, and they went and got the bodies. I think that's a brave and kind thing to do, friends.

The word is fast. The men of Jabesh “…buried their bones under the oak in Jabesh and fasted seven days.” (1 Chronicles 10:12) Fasting means going without food, so they stopped eating for that stretch. I think that shows how deeply they grieved. It's a quiet, faithful ending to a rough scene, friends.

The reason is that he was unfaithful to the LORD. Chronicles says it outright: “So Saul died for his unfaithfulness to the LORD…” (1 Chronicles 10:13) The writer names it directly, so there's no guessing. After all the battle, we get the reason, friends.

The answer is True. The writer says Saul “…even consulted a medium for guidance…” (1 Chronicles 10:13) That's one of the reasons given for his unfaithfulness. A medium is someone who claims to speak with the dead. The next verse goes on to say he failed to inquire of the LORD. (1 Chronicles 10:14)

The kingdom goes to David son of Jesse. The LORD “…turned the kingdom over to David son of Jesse.” (1 Chronicles 10:14) The writer says it goes to David, friends. Saul's story closes, and David's is coming.
